record.title: Higher-dimensional Balinski-type connectivity conjecture for cell complexes
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal C}$ be a $d$-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay regular cell complex with the intersection property. For each $k$, let ${\mathcal G}_k({\mathcal C})$ be the simple graph whose vertices are the $k$-dimensional cells of ${\mathcal C}$, with two cells adjacent when they are contained in a common $(k+1)$-dimensional cell.

**Higher-dimensional Balinski-type connectivity conjecture.** The graph ${\mathcal G}_k({\mathcal C})$ is

$$
(k+1)(d-k)
$$

-connected if $0\leq k\leq d-3$, and is $d$-connected if $k=d-2$.

This statement generalizes Balinski's theorem and the cited theorem of Fløystad, which is the case $k=0$. The source presents it as a statement following the known $k=0$ case; no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Piecewise linearity of the Freiman dimension function and constancy of the covering function
record.statement:
Let $F(K)$ and $G(K)$ be the functions introduced earlier in the paper for measuring the linear structure of finite binary sets with doubling parameter $K$. **The piecewise-linearity and piecewise-constancy conjecture.** For $K\geq 1$,

$$
F(K)\text{ is a piecewise linear function, and }G(K)\text{ is a piecewise constant function.}
$$

This conjecture proposes a global structural description of the two functions arising in the study of small-doubling binary sets. The supplied context does not define $F(K)$ and $G(K)$ or provide evidence concerning the conjecture's resolution.

record.title: Tight-neighborly triangulations are tight
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a triangulation of a connected sum of sphere bundles $S^{(d-1)}\times S^1$ and $S^{(d-1)}\text{$\times\hspace{-1.62ex}\_\hspace{-.4ex}\_\hspace{.7ex}$}S^1$ that is tight-neighborly, meaning that the relevant vertex bound is attained. A simplicial complex is **tight** over a field $\mathbb{K}$ if every induced homology map from a vertex-induced subcomplex to the whole complex is injective. **Tight-neighborliness conjecture.** Every tight-neighborly triangulation is tight.
The source notes that the conjecture was settled in even dimensions $d\geq4$ by Effenberger; the general assertion, including the remaining dimensions and hypotheses, is not resolved here.

record.title: Infinite log-concavity conjecture for longest-increasing-subsequence polynomials
record.statement: For each $n\geq 1$, let $P_n(x)=\sum_k P_{n,k}x^k$, where $P_{n,k}$ is the number of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. A polynomial is **infinitely log-concave** when every polynomial obtained by iterating the log-concavity operator remains log-concave. **Infinite log-concavity conjecture.** $P_n(x)$ is infinitely log-concave for $n\geq 1$. This strengthens the preceding log-concavity proposal for the longest-increasing-subsequence distribution; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, “Log-concavity and q-Log-convexity Conjectures on the Longest Increasing Subsequences of Permutations”, arXiv:0806.3392 (2008).

record.title: Infinite q-log-convexity conjecture for longest-increasing-subsequence polynomials
record.statement: For each $n\geq 1$, let $P_n(x)=\sum_k P_{n,k}x^k$, where $P_{n,k}$ is the number of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. A polynomial sequence is **infinitely q-log-convex** when every iterate of the relevant $q$-log-convexity operator is $q$-log-convex. **Infinite $q$-log-convexity conjecture.** The polynomial sequence $\{P_n(x)\}$ is infinitely $q$-log-convex. This proposes an iterated $q$-analogue of log-convexity for longest-increasing-subsequence polynomials; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: Infinite q-log-convexity conjecture for matching crossing-number polynomials
record.statement: For each $n\geq 1$, let $M_{2n}(x)=\sum_k M_{2n,k}x^k$, where $M_{2n,k}$ is the number of matchings on $[2n]$ with crossing number $k$. A polynomial sequence is **infinitely q-log-convex** when every iterate of the relevant $q$-log-convexity operator is $q$-log-convex. **Infinite $q$-log-convexity conjecture.** The polynomial sequence $\{M_{2n}(x)\}$ is infinitely $q$-log-convex. Furthermore, the polynomials $M_{2n}(x)$ are log-concave of any order with respect to infinitely $q$-log-convexity. This is the paper's strongest stated regularity proposal for matching crossing-number polynomials; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: The circuit-relation ideal conjecture for 3-connected matroid extensions
record.statement:
Let ${\mathbb{P}}$ be a partial field, let $M$ be a 3-connected ${\mathbb{P}}$-representable matroid, and let $N=M{-} e$ be a 3-connected deletion that settles $M$. Let $I_{N,M}$ be the ideal describing the quotient from the representation ring of $N$ to that of $M$, and let $\operatorname{Cr}(N)$ denote the relevant set of cross-ratios of $N$. **Circuit-relation ideal conjecture.** If $N=M{-} e$, $N$ and $M$ are 3-connected, and $N$ settles $M$, then $I_{N,M}$ is an ideal generated by relations $p-q$, where $p,q\in\operatorname{Cr}(N)$.

This conjecture proposes that the constraints imposed by extending a settled 3-connected matroid are generated by pairwise relations between cross-ratios of the smaller matroid. The source gives no evidence that the claim has been resolved.

record.title: The t-intersecting multiset conjecture
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let a $k$-multiset on $[n]$ be a multiset of cardinality $k$ whose elements lie in $[n]$. Two multisets are **$t$-intersecting** when their intersection has size at least $t$, counted with multiplicity. Let $n\geq n_0(k,t)$. **The $t$-intersecting multiset conjecture.** If $\mathcal{M}$ is a $t$-intersecting collection of $k$-multisets on $[n]$, then

$$
|\mathcal{M}|\leq \binom{n+k-t-1}{k-t}.
$$

Furthermore, equality is achieved if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is a trivial collection. This proposes the corresponding Erdős–Ko–Rado-type extremal bound for multisets; the source presents it as an additional direction and gives no resolution.

record.title: Snevily's conjecture for finite abelian groups of odd order
record.statement: Let $G$ be a multiplicatively written abelian group of odd order, and let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$ be two $k$-subsets of $G$. **Snevily's conjecture.** There is a permutation $\pi\in S_k$ such that $a_1b_{\pi(1)},\ldots,a_kb_{\pi(k)}$ are distinct. This conjecture concerns distinct representatives in products of two subsets of an abelian group; the paper notes that it is known for cyclic groups of odd order and that its validity follows from the determinant conjecture stated later for general finite abelian groups.

record.title: Conjecture on the number of projection cones defining maximal cells in equidistant tree space
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Q}_n$ be the space whose maximal cells arise from projection cones associated with equidistant trees, and let a **maximal cell** mean a maximal-dimensional cell of $\mathcal{Q}_n$. A **projection cone** is the cone of data vectors that orthogonally project onto a given non-degenerate equidistant tree.

**Projection-cone bound conjecture.** Every maximal cell in $\mathcal{Q}_n$ is obtained as the intersection of at most $(n-1)!$ projection cones.

The preceding theorem shows that some maximal cells are intersections of at least $(n-1)!$ projection cones, so the conjecture would make this bound sharp. The source gives no proof of the upper bound.

record.title: The alternating-sign recurrence conjecture for spanning trees of graph products
record.statement: Let $G$ be any graph, and write $G_n=G\times P_n$. Let $T_n$ denote the number of spanning trees of $G_n$, which satisfies a linear recurrence by the preceding result. **Alternating-sign recurrence conjecture.** The recurrence for $\{T_n\}$ has coefficients that alternate in sign. This conjecture predicts a sign pattern for the linear recurrences governing spanning-tree counts of graph products with paths; the source provides no evidence of resolution.

record.title: The complete-graph product recurrence order conjecture
record.statement: Let $K_k$ be the complete graph on $k$ vertices, let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, and consider the spanning-tree recurrence for the graph product $K_k\times P_n$. **Complete-graph product recurrence order conjecture.** The recurrence for the graph $K_k\times P_n$ has order $k$. This predicts an exact recurrence order for spanning-tree counts of complete-graph products with paths; the source provides no evidence of resolution.

record.title: Positivity conjecture for coefficients of the graph series $R_g$
record.statement:
Let $A_n$ be the weighted Laplacian matrix with off-diagonal entries $-w_{ij}$ and diagonal entries $\sum_i w_{ij}$, and define

$$
r_n({\mathbf{w}})=\operatorname{Tr}\ln\phi(A_n),\qquad R_n({\mathbf{w}})=\exp(r_n({\mathbf{w}}))=\det\phi(A_n),
$$

where $\phi(t)=\sinh(t/2)/(t/2)$. Let $R_g=(R_{g,n})_{n\geq 1}$ denote the homogeneous degree-$2g$ part of $R_n$, regarded as an element of the graph space $\mathcal{W}$, and write $R_g=\sum C_GG$.

**Positivity conjecture.** All the coefficients $C_G$ of the elements $R_g\in\mathcal{W}$ are positive.

This conjecture concerns the coefficientwise positivity of the exponential graph series arising from the determinant of the matrix function $\phi(A_n)$. The supplied text gives no resolution or further evidence, so its status remains open.

record.title: Coefficientwise q-unimodality conjecture for refined Eulerian polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ with exactly $k$ parts of size $1$, and write $A_{\lambda}^{{\rm maj},{\rm des},{\rm exc}}(q,p,t)$ as a polynomial in $p$ and $t$. **Coefficientwise $q$-unimodality conjecture.** The coefficient of $p^dt^j$ in

$$
A_{\lambda}^{{\rm maj},{\rm des},{\rm exc}}(q,p,t)
$$

is $q$-unimodal. This is suggested after the source establishes the corresponding $q$-symmetry, but no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: John Shareshian and Michelle L. Wachs, “Eulerian quasisymmetric functions”, arXiv:0812.0764 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.0764

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2008). “This conjecture was recently proved jointly with A. Henderson. See Section (New developments).} Let $\lambda \vdash n$. For all $j=0,1,\dots,n-1$, the Eulerian quasisymmetric function $Q_{\lambda,j}$ is Schur positive.”

record.title: Conjectured explicit system of parameters for graph invariant rings
record.statement:
For $n\ge3$, let $\mathcal{I}_n$ be the invariant ring on the edge variables $x_{\{i,j\}}$ and vertex variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$. A **system of parameters** is a homogeneous algebraically independent set over which $\mathcal{I}_n$ is finite as a module.

**Explicit parameter-system conjecture.** If $n\ge3$, the following invariants form a system of parameters for $\mathcal{I}_n$:

$$
x_{\{1,2\}}+\dots+x_{\{n-1,n\}},\quad \dots,\quad x_{\{1,2\}}^{\binom{n-1}{2}}+\dots+x_{\{n-1,n\}}^{\binom{n-1}{2}},
$$

$$
X_1+\dots+X_n,\quad\dots,\quad X_1^n+\dots+X_n^n.
$$

The construction is motivated by decomposing the representation into components and combining parameter systems for their invariant rings. It is known for $n=3,4,5$; the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for card values in two-person whist
record.statement: Consider two-person whist without the assumption of symmetry, where a player may force the opponent to discard by leading a suit in which the opponent is void. Cards are compared within the same suit according to their game-theoretic value. **Monotonicity conjecture.** A higher card is always at least as good as a smaller card in the same suit. This would provide a basic order property for card values in the more complicated nonsymmetric version of whist, whose analysis lies outside the scope of the current theory.

record.title: Thiéry's maximal-rank conjecture for the forest-tree incidence matrix
record.statement:
For $n\geq 2$, let $M_n=(m_{f,a})_{f,a}$ be the incidence matrix whose rows are indexed by labeled forests $f$ on $n$ vertices with $n-2$ edges and whose columns are indexed by trees $a$ on $n$ vertices, hence with $n-1$ edges. Set $m_{f,a}=1$ if $f$ is a subgraph of $a$. In the unlabeled case, let $m_{f,a}$ be the number of occurrences of $f$ in $a$.

**Thiéry's conjecture.** The labeled matrix $M_n$ has maximal rank, with linearly independent rows. The same conclusion holds in the unlabeled case.

The source says that the unlabeled assertion is a corollary of the labeled one and presents this as a preferred conjecture arising from work on algebraic graph reconstruction. Partial results are mentioned, but no resolution is given.

record.title: Bandlow–Schilling–Thiéry's uniqueness conjecture for affine promotion
record.statement:
Let $A_n$-crystals be the combinatorial crystals of type $A_n$, and consider tensor products of such crystals whose factors have rectangular shape. An affine structure of type $A_n^{(1)}$ is obtained by extending the finite crystal with the affine operators, equivalently by specifying the promotion operator.

**Bandlow–Schilling–Thiéry's conjecture.** There is a unique promotion operator, and hence a unique good affine structure of type $A_n^{(1)}$, on tensor products of type $A_n$ crystal graphs of rectangular shape.

For a single rectangular tableau crystal, promotion gives the affine operator through Schützenberger's jeu de taquin. The conjecture asks for uniqueness on tensor products; the source reports a proof for two factors but leaves the general case as the objective.

record.title: Relation between forcibly k-tough and forcibly k-factor graphical degree conditions
record.statement:
Let $pi=(d_1\leq\dots\leq d_n)$ be a graphical degree sequence. Let $k\geq2$ be an integer with $n>k+1$ and $kn$ even. The paper defines forcibly $k$-tough graphical sequences using the stated best monotone condition, Theorem~, and forcibly $k$-factor graphical sequences using Theorem~.

**Toughness-to-factor conjecture.** If $pi$ is forcibly $k$-tough graphical by Theorem~, then $pi$ is forcibly $k$-factor graphical by Theorem~.

This conjecture is motivated by the classical implication that a $k$-tough graph has a $k$-factor when the order and parity conditions hold. The authors report computational evidence for a relation between the two degree conditions, but do not prove the asserted implication.

record.title: The Brualdi–Ryser conjecture for partial transversals in latin squares
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a latin square of order $n$. A **near transversal** is a partial transversal of size $n-1$, and a **transversal** is a partial transversal of size $n$.

**Brualdi–Ryser conjecture.** Every latin square $L$ of order $n$ possesses a near transversal, and if $n$ is odd then $L$ possesses a transversal.

These are longstanding conjectures on the existence of large partial transversals in latin squares. The source explains that the chromatic number conjecture would imply them; their status remains open.
